title: Parasitic plant development: a new chemical inhibitor of Striga haustoria development
content: Approximately 1% of angiosperms are defined as parasitic plants that rely on other plants for sustenance (Westwood et al. 2010). Parasitic plants have independently evolved at least 12 times, and in all cases parasitism depends on the haustorium, a specialized organ that extracts water and nutrients from a host plant (Westwood et al. 2010; Yoshida et al. 2016). Some parasitic plants, such as those in the Striga genus, are noxious weeds in agriculture. For example, the most agriculturally damaging species, Striga hermonthica, parasitizes crops including rice, sorghum, and millet and decimates the yield of resource-poor farmers in Sub-Saharan Africa (Scholes and Press 2008).
